- Model consistently underestimates prices in early forecast windows, especially after sharp spikes or volatility; adjust downward bias for first 5–7 days.
- Overshoots occur after large upward spikes in history; cap forecast peaks at 10–15% above recent high for 3–5 days.
- Mean reversion is strong in 10–14 day horizons; if forecast is >15% above 10-day moving average, reduce by 5–8% for next 3–5 days.
- Sentiment history is flat (all 0.00) — no behavioral signal — so ignore sentiment-driven adjustments; rely on price momentum and volatility clustering.
- If true outcome shows sudden drop after spike (e.g., 48.25 → 35.94), model tends to overcorrect; reduce forecast by 5–10% for next 3–7 days.
- Horizon-specific: 30-day forecasts are prone to lagging; if true outcome shows strong downward trend after 10–12 days, reduce forecast by 3–6% per day for next 5–7 days.
- Avoid overfitting to recent history; if last 3–5 days are volatile, don’t extrapolate upward; use 10-day average as anchor for correction.
